summary: Chris Wilson's Independent Travel guide rounds up seven top Canadian ski resorts: Whistler Blackcomb, Tremblant, Sunshine Village, Fernie, Big White, Lake Louise and Revelstoke. Each entry covers terrain by ability level, village and apres atmosphere, and a sample package holiday with operator, hotel, price and departure date for the 2023-24 season. The piece pitches Canada for reliable snow, long seasons and options for every level of skier.
one_line: The Independent's guide to seven top Canadian ski resorts, with terrain details, village character and sample package holidays with prices for winter 2023-24.
key_facts: Whistler Blackcomb is the largest ski resort in North America, with over 8,100 acres of skiable terrain and over 200 runs, about 55 per cent of them intermediate.
Heidi offers a package to The Westin Resort & Spa in Whistler from £3,073pp for seven nights room-only with flights from London Heathrow to Vancouver, departing 13 January 2024.
Tremblant is Quebec's premier ski resort; its purpose-built village is styled on Old Quebec and offers ice skating, ice fishing and a casino.
British Airways Holidays offers the Fairmont Tremblant, a ski-in/ski-out hotel, from £1,329pp for seven nights with flights to Montreal, departing 20 January 2024.
Sunshine Village has over 3,000 acres, lies about 20 minutes from Banff, and its season typically runs from mid-November to late May.
Inghams offers the four-star Moose Hotel & Suites in Banff from £1,482pp for seven nights with flights to Calgary, departing 27 January 2024.
Fernie covers 2,500 acres, gets an average of nine metres of snowfall annually, and is best for advanced skiers thanks to ungroomed steep terrain and tree skiing.
Ski Solutions offers Lizard Creek Lodge in Fernie from £1,795pp including car hire, departing 30 December 2023.
Big White is a 2,800-acre resort in the Okanagan Highlands marketed as 'Canada's favourite family resort', with 119 runs, over 50 per cent for intermediates and 18 per cent for beginners.
Ski Safari's February half-term trip to Chateau Big White costs from £1,280pp for two adults and two children under 12, departing 10 February 2024.
Lake Louise has a larger ski area than Sunshine Village and views of Mount Assiniboine; the 'Ski Big 3' lift pass covers Lake Louise, Sunshine Village and Mount Norquay.
Crystal Ski offers Chateau Lake Louise from £1,904pp for seven nights with flights to Calgary, departing 27 January 2024.
Revelstoke opened in 2007; about 3,000 of an intended 8,000 acres are open, and its 1,700-metre vertical on Mount Mackenzie is the longest on the continent.
Ski Safari offers The Sutton Place hotel in Revelstoke from £2,455pp for 10 nights, departing 15 January 2024, with heli-skiing giving access to 500,000 acres and 400 runs.
